category_title: Students who internalize school-ascribed negative labels despite high engagement in elective contexts
student_description: This student presents a dual identity: they are an avid reader of self-selected texts but actively refuse required reading and traditional comprehension tasks. They internalize negative school-sanctioned labels (e.g., 'slow reader', 'ADHD') and are highly triggered by time pressure, speed expectations, and the analytical 'ripping apart' of texts.

criteria.rationale: Time limits and speed expectations trigger intense pressure and task refusal for this student, who needs space to visualize and process the text at their own pace.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly removes time limits or speed expectations, and avoids any fluency-focused drills or pacing demands.

criteria.rationale: The student heavily internalizes school-sanctioned labels like 'slow reader' or 'ADHD' and needs active encouragement to question the authority of these deficit-based identities.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts the student to question, challenge, or reframe their negative self-labels rather than accepting or reinforcing them as fixed deficits.

criteria.rationale: The student resents 'ripping apart' texts for traditional comprehension questions but thrives when allowed to build a 'movie in their head' and think holistically.
criteria.check: The tutor encourages personal connection, visualization, or holistic understanding of the text, explicitly avoiding traditional, drill-based comprehension questions.
